root_cause: Header echoes mini_cart HTML without an explicit trusted-renderer contract, so Plugin Check cannot prove the already-escaped adapter HTML is safe.
concrete_action: Keep WooCommerce Adapter as the sole mini-cart HTML renderer. Do not blanket wp_kses_post() if it strips Woo data attributes. Add a narrowly justified PHPCS suppression at the call site only after confirming every dynamic value in render_mini_cart_body() is escaped/kses-ed. Prefer renaming context key to mini_cart_html only if it improves clarity without churn.
regression_prevention: Add a focused static/runtime contract proving mini-cart dynamic name/url/variation/price/subtotal are escaped or kses-ed and header never echoes arbitrary user/meta HTML.
rule_candidate: Trusted HTML may be emitted unescaped only when produced by a canonical Gloskin/Woo renderer that escapes all dynamic values; the call site must carry a narrow documented suppression.
acceptance_criteria: Plugin Check no longer reports this finding; cart fragments/remove links still work; no data-* attributes are stripped.
notes: Not currently evidence of exploitable XSS because renderer escapes dynamic values; treat as trust-boundary hardening, not redesign.

root_cause: save_meta() reads dynamic $_POST values and relies on registered post-meta sanitizers during update_post_meta(), but the sanitization boundary is implicit and invisible to static analysis.
concrete_action: Make sanitization explicit before persistence. Reuse registered meta contracts via sanitize_meta($key, $value, 'post', $post->post_type) or an equally native field-aware path; keep nonce/capability checks. Do not duplicate sanitization rules in a parallel schema.
regression_prevention: Add admin-meta contract test: unslashed posted strings/arrays/integers are passed through registered/native sanitization before update_post_meta(); nonce/capability remain mandatory.
rule_candidate: State-changing admin input must be explicitly validated/sanitized before persistence even when registered meta also sanitizes on write.
acceptance_criteria: Four scanner warnings disappear; existing rich text/URLs/phones/relationships/gallery/meta behavior remains unchanged.
notes: Current registered meta callbacks are a mitigating control; this task makes the input boundary explicit.

root_cause: REQUEST_URI is unslashed and compared for active-path detection without an explicit sanitization step.
concrete_action: Sanitize the unslashed REQUEST_URI with an appropriate text/path-safe WordPress sanitizer before strtok/path comparison. Do not change routing or introduce redirect logic.
regression_prevention: Add navigation contract for query strings and hostile/encoded request input; active item calculation must remain deterministic and output-free.
rule_candidate: Superglobal reads must be unslashed then sanitized before use, including non-output comparison paths.
acceptance_criteria: Warning disappears; fallback navigation active-state behavior is unchanged for normal routes and query strings.

concrete_action: Mechanically rename top-level template variables and foreach aliases to $gloskin_* names. Do not wrap templates in new classes/functions and do not alter context keys or markup.

rule_candidate: Every variable introduced at top level in plugin template files must use the gloskin_ prefix; function-local variables are exempt.

root_cause: Plugin Check sees apply_filters('the_content', ...) as an unprefixed plugin hook, but the_content is a WordPress core hook intentionally invoked for canonical page content rendering.
concrete_action: Do NOT rename the hook. Add a narrow PHPCS suppression on that invocation with a comment stating it is the WordPress core the_content filter.
regression_prevention: Add contract asserting the canonical core the_content filter remains invoked and no Gloskin duplicate content hook is introduced.
rule_candidate: First-party hooks must be prefixed; deliberate calls to documented WordPress/Woo core hooks are exempt and require a local justification when a sniff cannot infer ownership.
acceptance_criteria: Finding is suppressed/closed while core content filtering behavior remains intact.
notes: True false-positive by ownership, not a code defect.

root_cause: WPCS treats dynamic RuntimeException messages as output, but these importer exceptions are transport-neutral domain errors. The admin AJAX boundary JSON-encodes them and the admin JS renders error.message with textContent, while server-rendered last_error uses esc_html(). Escaping inside the domain exception would encode transport semantics too early.
concrete_action: Do NOT esc_html() exception payloads in the importer/bundle. Add one narrowly scoped phpcs:disable/enable for ExceptionNotEscaped around the relevant class/body with a strong rationale, or equivalent minimal suppressions. Preserve strict bundle validation.
regression_prevention: Add error-boundary contract proving AJAX errors are JSON responses, admin JS uses textContent (never innerHTML), and server-rendered last_error uses esc_html().
rule_candidate: Escape at the final output context, not inside domain exceptions. ExceptionNotEscaped may be suppressed only when every presentation boundary is separately proven safe.
acceptance_criteria: 61 scanner errors are intentionally suppressed/closed without HTML entities leaking into JSON messages; importer error UX remains readable and safe.
notes: Do not cargo-cult escape RuntimeException strings; that would violate late-escaping discipline.

root_cause: Temporary/runtime cleanup uses direct unlink()/rmdir() despite WordPress filesystem APIs.
concrete_action: Replace file deletes with wp_delete_file(). For the fixed confined runtime directory, prefer the smallest WordPress-native directory removal that does not introduce credential prompts or a new filesystem service; if WP_Filesystem would make this one-shot AJAX cleanup less reliable, retain only the directory rmdir with a narrowly documented suppression after all declared files are removed.
regression_prevention: Extend sample-import cleanup contract: only confined runtime paths are removed; consumed state persists before cleanup; cleanup failure stays non-destructive; no direct unlink remains.
rule_candidate: Use WordPress file deletion APIs for files. Direct directory removal is allowed only for a fixed confined one-shot runtime path with an explicit documented exception when WP_Filesystem would alter runtime semantics.
acceptance_criteria: No direct unlink findings; directory finding is either eliminated safely or explicitly justified; cleanup/retry/consumed contracts remain green.
notes: Do not create a generic filesystem abstraction.

root_cause: Bundle URL validation uses PHP parse_url() instead of WordPress wp_parse_url().
concrete_action: Replace parse_url() with wp_parse_url() while preserving the same host/path validation and rejection behavior.
regression_prevention: Add/retain bundle validation cases for malformed URL, wrong host, and valid HTTPS source URL.
rule_candidate: Use wp_parse_url() for WordPress plugin URL parsing.
acceptance_criteria: Both findings disappear; bundle source URL validation behavior is unchanged.

acceptance_criteria: Five findings disappear; importer identity/verification tests remain green.

root_cause: One-shot importer uses post-meta identity/provenance queries. Meta-value queries are not ideal for large public hot paths, but this workflow is administrator-only, bounded to 13 parents/10 variations/58 attachments, temporary, and intentionally avoids custom tables.
concrete_action: Keep native get_posts()/meta identity queries. Add narrow PHPCS suppressions on meta_key/meta_value lines with the bounded one-shot rationale. Do not create a custom table/index or raw SQL merely to silence the scanner.
regression_prevention: Existing contract must continue to prove exact object counts, unique source identities, checkpointing, and no public importer endpoint.

acceptance_criteria: Warnings are intentionally suppressed/closed; no architecture expansion; importer remains bounded and admin-only.
notes: Architecture exception, not a performance bug at current scale.
